newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tycoon Li vague on Cheung Kong reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Tycoon Li vague on Cheung Kong reshuffle.

text.p: Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing's flagship business group announced a corporate restructuring on Monday affecting his China infrastructure firm and Hong Kong electricity utility.
But Li described the changes as merely a move to streamline operations and better allocate resources.

"The immediate benefit of the reorganisation is the streamlining of the Cheung Kong group's infrastructure business. There will be no change in the operations or management of any of the companies involved," Li told a news conference.
"The new structure will allow us to allocate resources and match areas of specialisation and management teams more efficiently," he said.

The restructuring involves all four of the group's listed companies -- parent Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, its 45 percent held associate Hutchison Whampoa, Hong Kong Electric Holdings Ltd and the newest member of the group, Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd.
On Friday, Hutchison bought Hongkong Electric shares to push its holding in the utility to 35.01 percent, cresting the exchange's takeover threshold and triggering a general offer.

Hutchison plans to transfer its 707.53 million shares in Hongkong Electric to Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI). The stake is valued at HK$18.74 billion, based on HK$26.50 per share, a five percent premium to Friday's closing price of HK$25.25.
CKI will fund the purchase of the stake in Hongkong Electric by issuing 886.21 million new shares to Hutchison at HK$21.15 per share, Friday's closing price.

Cheung Kong will transfer its 70.66 percent holding in CKI to Hutchison, valued at HK$20.45 billion based on CKI's Friday closing price. Hutchison will satisfy the purchase with the issue of 349.50 million new shares to Cheung Kong.

The proposed new shareholding structure would have Cheung Kong holding 50.17 percent of Hutchison, compared with 45.36 percent at present. Hutchison would hold 84.6 percent of CKI from 3.93 percent now.
CKI would go from no holding in Hongkong Electric to 35.01 percent if no acceptance is received under the offer, and 50.01 percent if Hutchison acquires 75 percent of the utility.

In the event that a necessary waiver, to be set out in a forthcoming announcement, was not obtained, Cheung Kong would receive 254.32 million new Hutchison shares and about HK$5.57 billion in cash, the group said in an announcement.
Additional details would be announced soon, it said.
One analyst said CKI would enjoy a steady cash flow from Hongkong Electric into its China development projects, many of which required long investment horizons.
"Hongkong Electric has more management skills," said Fred Kam, investment analyst at New China Hong Kong Securities. "It is a big bonus for Cheung Kong Infrastructure."
But other analysts disagreed.
"I think the move will have a negative impact on CKI," said Geoffrey Cheng, Hong Kong and China infrastructure analyst at NAVA SC Securities.
But Li dismissed worries that increasing CKI's stake in slow-growing Hongkong Electric would dilute and affect earnings of the profitable group.
"The restructuring will benefit all companies," Li said.

The benefit to Hutchison would be a boost in 1997 earnings from exceptional gains on the sale of its Hongkong Electric shares. Brokers said the company was believed to have acquired them at around HK$5.00 per share in 1985.
Trading in the shares of the four listed companies was suspended on Monday.
